1. Map 50x larger — in normalized coords, the map is fixed size; but "50 times larger" means the world/terrain area in world units. Currently WORLD=224, VIEW_SIZE=160. Simplest: make the terrain 50x the area (linear scale sqrt(50)≈7.07) → WORLD ~1584, VIEW_SIZE same → camera zoom out more. But then unit sizes fixed relative to terrain, so buildings look tiny. Alternatively, redefine coordinates: currently normalized 0..1 across the world. Map 50x larger area means the same screen view shows a smaller fraction of the map, so camera zoom needs to allow zooming out much further and panning.

A cleaner approach: keep units/entities in *world* units, expand map dimensions, drop normalized coordinates... but that's a big refactor of game.js. Alternatively, keep normalized coordinates and enlarge world dimensions, scaling entity models by the same factor so relative proportions are preserved, and adjust gameplay ranges (which are in pixels via distance()) accordingly.

Let me think in terms of the existing system:
- Positions stored normalized 0..1.
- distance(a,b) computes screen pixels: (dx * scale * width) where scale = camera.z * MAP_SCALE, MAP_SCALE=224/160=1.4.
- Camera z from .55 to 2.2, initial 1.5. World 224 wide, view 160. So at z=1, the visible width fraction = 1/(1*1.4) ≈ 0.714 of world... Plan: Introduce a MAP_SCALE that gives zoom levels showing a smaller fraction. Let's increase world to e.g. 1600 units and keep entity models at world-size scale ~ scaled by 7.07 to match proportion? Hmm, but then the camera ortho view size 160 shows tiny area.

Let me reframe: rather than physically scaling the ground geometry (which affects visual only), the key gameplay change is the coordinate mapping and the amount of visible area. The world plane can just be enlarged (say 50x area = linear 7.07x) with terrain texture repeated, decorations spread, and models scaled up 7.07x so they occupy the same fraction of the map as before (buildings remain visually same relative size vs. map... no wait, that makes them the same apparent size on-screen when zoomed to same fraction).

Actually, what does "map 50 times larger" mean for gameplay? More space to maneuver, longer travel times, room for large bases. If everything scales uniformly by 7x (map, units, ranges, speeds), the game plays identically, just zoomed out. That's not what they want.

What they want: a much bigger map with more room around bases, so enemy base far away, time to build up. So the map should be much larger relative to unit/building sizes. That means: keep unit/building pixel sizes and ranges similar, but expand the map area 50x. Travel distances get much longer. Speeds should perhaps increase a bit but the point is a big map.

So implementation: 
- Keep normalized positions but make the world/terrain larger physically (linear ×~7.07) and keep buildings/units at roughly the same world-unit size (they'd appear smaller relative to map, which is what "map is 50x larger" means). But on screen, when zoomed in to see a base, entities need to be legible. So the view must zoom to a comparable "fraction" — camera z range should allow zooming in on a small area.

Let's define: world linear = 224 * 7.07 ≈ 1584. Keep entity sizes in world units the same (buildings ~14 units wide, units ~5 units) — now they're 1/7 the relative size. Camera view size 160 world units shows 10% of the map width — that's a decent tactical view where a base spans maybe 100 units.
